_note: Animals the Mexica kept and hunted: turkey flock, dog pack, deer hunt and fowling as joint-product recipes (Complaints/654), after the herd pattern of 95_herds.json. Each recipe is keyed by one of its products.

feather_kg.basis: per flock of 100 turkeys kept for a year (turkey_kg)
feather_kg.yield_basis: TURKEY FLOCK, meat, fat and feathers from the same birds. Every figure is the species row's in data/world/living_stock.json times 100 head; its source field names what was read (Wikipedia wild-turkey weights and clutch size; Speller et al. 2018 on maize-fed Postclassic turkeys) and which figures are labelled heuristics with no source found. Carcass = slaughtered birds x live weight x dressing fraction, of which rendered fat is fat_kg and the rest meat_kg; feathers are a share of live weight. Maize is the ration. Labour is a keeper tending 200 birds at 2400 hours a keeper-year (no source found, a labelled heuristic) plus plucking and dressing each bird. No land entry: a yard flock fed from the household store. Conf D throughout; the cost is split by mass (sim/prices/joint_allocation.py, retire: Complaints/507). herd_stock is the live weight of the 100 birds kept. PASS 9 (Complaint 671): opened en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wild_turkey (adult males 7.6 kg, females 4.26 kg average from two large studies) and extension.umaine.edu/publications/2223e (commercial turkey dressing 77 to 81 percent, no feather, blood or fat shares). The species figures live in data/world/living_stock.json (owned by Complaints/532) and were not changed here; feather share, fat share, keeper ratio and ration remain without an opened source. Stays D.

hide_kg.basis: per pack of 100 dogs kept for a year (dog_kg)
hide_kg.yield_basis: DOG PACK, meat, fat and skins from the animals eaten. Every figure is the species row's in data/world/living_stock.json times 100 head; the row's source is a museum note citing Sahagun (Florentine Codex 9:48: dogs bought 'to provide the people as food') and nothing else was found, so weight, offtake, dressing, fat and hide shares, ration and keeper ratio are labelled heuristics (conf D, no source found). Carcass = eaten dogs x live weight x dressing fraction, split into fat_kg and meat_kg; the skin is a share of live weight. Fed maize scraps. Labour as the turkey flock. Cost split by mass (retire: Complaints/507). herd_stock is the live weight of the 100 dogs kept. PASS 9: no page on dog weight, dressing, fat or skin share was found beyond the museum note already cited. Stays D.

fat_kg.basis: per 100 deer taken: boneless venison, trimmed fat and raw skins
fat_kg.yield_basis: HUNT. Meat per deer is from Ohio Division of Wildlife, Venison Meat Yield (https://dam.assets.ohio.gov/image/upload/ohiodnr.gov/documents/wildlife/wild-ohio-harvest-community/Venison%20Yield.pdf, opened): 'The average deer weighed 107.56 pounds field dressed and yielded 52.19 pounds of venison, or a 48.52% meat yield' (115 white-tailed deer, 2017, boneless venison after butchering): 23.67 kg boneless venison from a deer of 48.79 kg field-dressed weight; boneless, so conservative beside the bone-in meat_kg of the herds, and a temperate-zone stand-in for the Mexican white-tailed deer, whose weight was not found. Trimmed fat is 4 percent and the raw skin 8 percent of field-dressed weight (both checked in PASS 11 below). The hunter's hours are the energy of the products at the hunter trade's return (data/world/trades.json trade 'hunter': 1115 kcal an hour, Kelly 2013, The Lifeways of Hunter-Gatherers ch. 3, the Ache average from hunting alone with search time; already in the repo at conf C, that page not re-opened here): venison 1500 kcal and fat 9000 kcal a kilogram over 1115 kcal an hour, plus 4 hours a carcass to flay and joint (all checked in PASS 11 below). The ceiling on what a place's wild game gives stays in the geography wild-game rows (data/world/geography/resources/animals.json) and the hunter hours cap (sim/labour/food_gathering.py); as with fish_kg the recipe books the hours and the schema has no siting field, so forest siting is carried by those rows. No land entry, so the stand pays no arable rent. Cost split by mass (retire: Complaints/507). PASS 9 (Complaint 671): opened en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-tailed_deer: a field-dressed buck of 183 kg was estimated at 232 kg alive, a dressed fraction of 0.79, which agrees with the 78 percent seen in a calculator summary. Hide share (a hunting guide gave 9 to 12 percent of weight, inconsistent between versions, search summary only) and trimmed fat (no page found) are not opened. PASS 11 (Complaint 671): opened deeranddeerhunting.com, Dan Schmidt, 'How Much Meat is On 1 Deer?' (https://www.deeranddeerhunting.com/blogs/dan-schmidt-deer-blog-whitetail-wisdom/how-much-meat-is-on-1-deer), a hunting blog, which lists hide factors as a share of live weight: adult doe (140 pounds) 7.9 percent, adult buck (160 pounds) 8.7 percent, bucks over 160 pounds 9 percent. The 8 percent of field-dressed weight used here is about 6.3 percent of live weight at the 0.79 dressed fraction, inside a factor of 1.5 of that range, so the skin share is sourced. Opened forums.bowhunting.com thread 'Those of you that process your own deer, how long is the process' (https://forums.bowhunting.com/threads/those-of-you-that-process-your-own-deer-how-long-is-the-process.16276), anecdotes: deboning and packaging one deer 1 to 5 hours ('about 2 hour job', 'about 4hrs by myself', 'about 5 hours for me alone'), so 4 hours a carcass for flaying and jointing is the same order. Opened en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_energy: fat 9 kcal per gram, so 9000 kcal a kilogram of fat is sourced. Fat: Robertson, Schaefer, Fortin and Landry (Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, Lacombe), 'Meat yield and quality: factors affecting venison yield and quality', Canadian Meat Science Association newsletter, September 2000 (https://www.cmsa-ascv.ca/documents/2000September-00RobertsonEtAlpgs10-13.pdf, opened): farmed white-tail deer carcasses averaged 71.8 percent lean, 9.6 percent readily dissectable fat (range down to 2.0 percent) and 18.6 percent bone, carcass 57.3 percent of live weight; cull breeding-herd animals, so fatter than a wild deer. Fat of 4 percent of field-dressed weight is 2.4 times below the 9.6 percent mean and inside the reported range, so it is kept. Venison energy: USDA FoodData Central via getfoodfacts.com, game meat deer ground raw (FDC 172602, https://getfoodfacts.com/food/game-meat-deer-ground-raw-172602) 157 kcal and 7.13 g fat per 100 g, and venison NFS (FDC 2705913, https://getfoodfacts.com/food/venison-nfs-2705913) 167 kcal per 100 g, so 1570 to 1670 kcal a kilogram against the 1500 used. Hunter return: Hawkes, O'Connell and Coxworth 2010, 'Family Provisioning Is Not the Only Reason Men Hunt', Current Anthropology (https://content.csbs.utah.edu/~hawkes/Hawkes_al10notJustprovisioningG&Hcorrec.pdf, opened), quoting Gurven and Hill 2009: 830 kcal per hour for Ache hunting, against 1115 here (factor 1.3). Arithmetic check: (2367.3 x 1500 + 195.154 x 9000) / 1115 = 4760 hours, plus 4 x 100 = 400, gives the 5160 hours stated. Every number in the row now has an opened page of the same order (blogs, forum anecdotes, a newsletter, a data aggregator).

down_kg.basis: per 100 kg live weight of wildfowl netted or snared on lake and marsh
down_kg.yield_basis: FOWLING. Wildfowl quantities, each checked in PASS 11 below against an opened page of the same order (the values themselves are the original author figures): 65 percent of live weight edible, 6 points of it fat, 5 percent feathers and down, hours at the hunter trade's return (data/world/trades.json trade 'hunter': 1115 kcal an hour, Kelly 2013, The Lifeways of Hunter-Gatherers ch. 3, the Ache average from hunting alone with search time; already in the repo at conf C, that page not re-opened here) with meat at 1500 and fat at 9000 kcal a kilogram, plus 0.25 hour per kilogram of bird to pluck and dress. Ceiling and siting as the hunt: the wild-game rows and the hunter hours cap. Cost split by mass (retire: Complaints/507). PASS 11 (Complaint 671), pages opened: Edible share: University of Wisconsin Extension, 'Bird Breakdown: Exploring Yields and Cuts of Poultry' (https://livestock.extension.wisc.edu/articles/bird-breakdown-exploring-yields-and-cuts-of-poultry) gives Pekin duck dressing at 65 to 70 percent of live weight and says a ready-to-cook carcass is 'around 60% meat and 40% skin and bones', so meat and skin of about 40 percent of live weight for a farm duck; the 65 percent edible (meat plus fat) used here is about 1.6 times that, a domestic-duck figure standing in for a wild bird. Fat: USDA FoodData Central record for wild duck breast, meat only, raw (via getfoodfacts.com, https://getfoodfacts.com/food/duck-wild-breast-meat-only-raw-174469) gives 4.25 g fat and 123 kcal per 100 g; 59 kg of meat at 4.25 percent is 2.5 kg of fat inside the meat, and the 6 kg here is 2.4 times that because it counts skin and body fat as well (skin-on wild duck is richer; that record was seen in a search snippet only). Down and feathers: Hopps 2002, 'Information on Waterfowl Feather Characteristics', Transactions of the Illinois State Academy of Science 95(3):229-237 (https://myisas.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/08/095-22MS2201-print.pdf, opened), ten duck species: plumage 5.5 percent of body mass on average, males 5.7 and females 5.3 percent, so 5 percent is sourced. Meat energy: the same USDA record, 123 kcal per 100 g, is 1230 kcal a kilogram against the 1500 used (factor 1.2). Fat energy: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food_energy (opened) gives fat 9 kcal per gram, so 9000 kcal a kilogram. Hunter return: Hawkes, O'Connell and Coxworth 2010, 'Family Provisioning Is Not the Only Reason Men Hunt', Current Anthropology (https://content.csbs.utah.edu/~hawkes/Hawkes_al10notJustprovisioningG&Hcorrec.pdf, opened) quote Gurven and Hill 2009 at 830 kcal per hour for Ache hunting, against 1115 here (factor 1.3). Plucking and dressing: waldeneffect.org, 'Pluck a duck' (https://www.waldeneffect.org/blog/Pluck_a_duck/, a blog; a commenter reports 'about 30 minutes per duck to pluck'), so for a bird of about a kilogram the 0.25 hour a kilogram used is half that time. Check of the arithmetic: 59 x 1500 + 6 x 9000 = 142,500 kcal / 1115 = 127.8 hours, plus 0.25 x 100 = 25 hours, 152.8 hours as stated. All pages are secondary, modern or hobbyist; none gives a wild-fowling catch rate, which the row does not use (the return rate stands in for it).

turkey_kg.basis: per 100 head kept for a year, output as kg of live weight added to the stock
turkey_kg.yield_basis: GROWN. 100 head at the row's live weight times its natural increase (rates and sources in data/world/living_stock.json; the products the head give meanwhile are in the recipe of this file that holds the stock). Labour is the keeper's year shared among the head a keeper tends, as in the sheep_kg entry. The ration is charged in the product recipe, not twice. No land: a household animal. Conf D. Made only where the stock is already held. PASS 9: increase and keeper hours come from the species row of data/world/living_stock.json (Complaints/532). Stays D.
